blocks.content: The Authority consists of a Chairperson, and not more than two whole-time members and not more than two part-time members, all appointed by the Central Government.

rows: Chairperson + Max 2 Whole-time + Max 2 Part-time Members

items: Tenure limit for TRAI Chairperson and members is 3 years or 65 years of age, whichever comes earlier.
The 2000 Amendment stripped TRAI of its adjudicatory powers and created the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT).
All appointments to TRAI are made directly by the Central Government.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: TRAI was established under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997 to regulate telecommunication services.
The body consists of a Chairperson, a maximum of two whole-time members, and a maximum of two part-time members appointed by the Central Government.
Members hold office for a term of three years or until reaching 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
The TRAI Amendment Act of 2000 separated adjudicatory functions from TRAI and transferred them to TDSAT.
Members must possess specialized knowledge or professional experience in telecommunications, industry, finance, law, or administration.
